children.name: Cinclus
children.description: Dippers — the only aquatic passerines. These stocky, dark-plumaged birds are perfectly adapted for life along fast-flowing streams. They walk and swim underwater, using their wings to 'fly' against the current while searching for insect larvae among the streambed stones. A transparent third eyelid (nictitating membrane) allows them to see underwater. Their loud, ringing song carries above the roar of rapids.

children.name: Cinclus cinclus
children.description: The white-throated dipper (Cinclus cinclus), also known as the European dipper or just dipper, is an aquatic, passerine bird found in Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Cinclus mexicanus
children.description: The American dipper (Cinclus mexicanus), also known as a water ouzel, is a semiaquatic bird species native from North America.

children.name: Cinclus leucocephalus
children.description: The white-capped dipper (Cinclus leucocephalus) is a semiaquatic passerine bird of South America.

children.name: Cinclus pallasii
children.description: thumb|Brown Dipper,Pahalgam, Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir The brown dipper (Cinclus pallasii), also known as Pallas's dipper, Asian dipper or the Asiatic dipper, is an aquatic songbird found in the mountains of the east Palearctic.

children.name: Cinclus schulzi
children.description: The rufous-throated dipper or Argentine dipper (Cinclus schulzii) is a Vulnerable species of semiaquatic songbird of South America.
